eligibility_reason: Windschitl & Wells (1998) introduce the alternative-outcomes effect with six new studies (casino night, cookie jar, classroom cleaner, hurricane, raffle sign-up, comparison preferences); none is presented as a replication of a separately published finding. Study 3's scenario and data were 'briefly described in a separate publication (Windschitl & Wells, 1996)', i.e. the same data re-reported, not new data, and the cross-study consistency is within-paper only.
